passage.title: A Second Chance
paras: Every year, thousands of teenagers in the UK appear before a youth court. For many, it is the lowest point of their lives so far. What happens next matters enormously.

Youth courts can order a young person to repair the harm they have caused: cleaning graffiti, working with a charity, or meeting the person they hurt and apologising. Supporters say this teaches responsibility far better than a cell does.

Of course, some crimes are so serious that a young person must be kept away from the public. But for most, a second chance is not weakness; it is common sense. A teenager who learns to make amends is far less likely to offend again than one who learns only to fear.

questions.q: Give two things a youth court can order a young person to do.
questions.a: Any two: clean graffiti; work with a charity; meet the person they hurt and apologise

questions.q: What is the writer's view of second chances? Explain how you know.
questions.a: The writer supports them: 'a second chance is not weakness; it is common sense'; they argue amends work better than fear

questions.q: Compare the article's idea of justice with Stanley's experience in Holes.
questions.a: For example: the article wants punishment that repairs harm; Stanley is sent to dig pointless holes, which only causes suffering, so Camp Green Lake is not this kind of justice

questions.q: Which word means 'making up for a past wrong': redemption, revenge or ridicule?
Is this sentence active or passive? 'The sneakers were taken by the police.'
Which tense is 'He had dug the hole'?
What do we call the first sentence of a paragraph that states its main point?
How does Sachar present the theme of justice in Holes? Use the PETZAAL steps: Point, Evidence, Technique, Zoom, Alternative, Author, Link. Start: 'Sachar presents justice as...'
questions.a: Award up to 10: Point (1), Evidence (1), Technique (1), Zoom on a word (2), Alternative interpretation (2), Author's purpose (2), Link to the question (1). For example: the Warden's cruelty is finally punished and Stanley's family curse is lifted, so justice arrives slowly but surely.
